label: Complaint
detail: Pain, pressure, tightness or discomfort in the chest, shoulders, arms, neck, back, upper abdomen or jaw; shortness of breath and fatigue count as equivalents.

label: History
detail: Pain characteristics, accompanying symptoms and cardiac risk factors.

label: Vitals and exam
detail: Sweating and fast breathing lean toward ACS, fast heart rate and dyspnea toward PE, air under the skin toward esophageal rupture; chest wall tenderness or pain on inspiration leans noncardiac.

label: 12-lead ECG
detail: Recorded and read within 10 minutes of arrival.

label: Complaint
detail: New or worsening breathlessness.

label: History
detail: Known heart failure, lung disease, VTE risk factors.

label: Exam
detail: Pain on inspiration and one-sided absent breath sounds point to pneumothorax; fever, localized pleuritic pain and dullness point to pneumonia.

label: First tests
detail: ECG, chest radiograph, natriuretic peptide.

label: Complaint
detail: Pain in the lower abdomen or pelvis; its location narrows the list.

label: Pregnancy status
detail: Urine or serum beta-hCG is the first step in women who could be pregnant.

label: Exam clues
detail: Migration from the umbilicus to the right lower quadrant suggests appendicitis; left lower quadrant tenderness suggests diverticulitis.

label: Patient group
detail: Adult, child or pregnant; this changes which imaging comes first.

label: Complaint
detail: New or different headache; how fast it reached peak intensity (peak within 1 hour matters for the SAH rule).

label: History: red flags
detail: SNNOOP10: systemic symptoms including fever, cancer history, neurologic deficit, sudden onset, onset after 65, new or changed pattern, positional, triggered by cough or exertion, papilledema, progressive, pregnancy, painful eye with autonomic features, trauma, immune compromise, painkiller overuse or new drug.

label: Exam
detail: Full neurologic exam, level of consciousness, neck pain or stiffness, limited neck flexion, papilledema, fever.

label: Signs of infection and vital signs
detail: Screened with NEWS/NEWS2, MEWS or SIRS rather than qSOFA alone.

label: Sepsis certainty
detail: The 2026 guideline grades suspected sepsis as definite, probable, possible or unlikely.

label: The event
detail: Prodrome, position (standing, sitting, supine), exertion, palpitations, triggers such as pain, cough, micturition or prolonged standing.

label: History
detail: Structural heart disease or prior myocardial infarction, family history of sudden cardiac death at a young age.

label: Exam
detail: Physical examination including lying and standing blood pressure.

label: 12-lead ECG
detail: Useful in the initial evaluation (class I).

label: Complaint
detail: Vomiting red blood or coffee-ground material, or black stools; bleeding from esophagus, stomach or duodenum.

label: Vitals and labs
detail: Inputs for the Glasgow-Blatchford score.

label: Complaint
detail: One-sided leg swelling or pain.

label: History
detail: Prior DVT or PE, cancer, recent immobilization; whether another diagnosis is as likely.

label: Timing and triggers
detail: Continuous for more than 24 hours (acute vestibular syndrome), triggered by position, or spontaneous episodes.

label: Exam
detail: Nystagmus, HINTS (head impulse, nystagmus, test of skew), gait, Dix-Hallpike when positional.

label: Complaint
detail: Sudden weakness, numbness, speech or vision loss.

label: Timing
detail: Time last known well decides treatment eligibility.

label: Bedside glucose
detail: Checked before thrombolysis; severe hypoglycemia or hyperglycemia can mimic stroke.

label: Duration
detail: Acute means 6 weeks or less.

label: Red flags
detail: New urinary retention or overflow incontinence, loss of anal tone or fecal incontinence, saddle anesthesia, progressive leg weakness; also cancer history, infection, fracture risk.

label: Complaint
detail: Sudden, colicky flank pain, often with blood in the urine.

label: History
detail: Known stones, pregnancy, signs of infection.
